subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Hypersonic Flight: Beyond Mach 5
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Hypersonic Flight: Beyond Mach 5.

hook.text: At Mach 5, air heats to 1,800 degrees Celsius. Molecules break apart. The air itself becomes chemically reactive.

buildup.text: Conventional jet engines can't function above Mach 3 — the incoming air is too hot for combustion to work normally.

discovery.text: Scramjets breathe supersonic air directly. They have no moving parts. The engine is essentially a shaped tube with fuel injectors.

twist.text: Scramjets can't start from rest. They need a rocket or jet engine to accelerate to Mach 4 before the scramjet can ignite.

climax.text: Hypersonic weapons and vehicles are being developed by the US, China, and Russia. The race is military, not commercial — yet.

punchline.text: No moving parts. No low-speed start. Just shaped air and injected fuel.

quiz.question: Why can't scramjets start from a standstill?
options: The fuel used in scramjets requires extreme heat to ignite properly
They need a rocket or jet to accelerate to about Mach 4 before supersonic airflow can sustain combustion
Scramjet structures would melt at low speeds due to insufficient airflow cooling
